description: Installation of 1No. BT Street Hub Unit and associated advertisement panels on either side of the unit
decision_conditions: <span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Verdana,Geneva,sans-serif">The proposed development, by reason of its size, scale, detailed design, location, and moving digital content, is likely to result in a distraction to drivers, thus failing to contribute to a safe road environment where traffic accident casualties are steadily reduced, supporting Vision Zero objectives. It fails to provide a permeable pedestrian environment that is easy and safe to walk through, and fails to mitigate the negative impact on the operation of transport infrastructure, contrary to policies T1 (Strategic approach to transport), T2 (Healthy streets), and T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) of the London Plan (2021) and policies LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), LP42 (Walking and Cycling), and LP43 (Transport and Development) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020).&nbsp;</span></span>

<span id="docs-internal-guid-ffb4f446-7fff-6afc-299f-c4f5706ed704"><p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;text-align: justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:12pt;padding:0pt 5pt 0pt 5pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">The proposed kiosk is situated on a stretch of pavement on Shoreditch High Street that contains heavy footfall, with many passengers boarding and alighting from nearby bus stops located on both sides of the road, in proximity to the application site, as well as crossing the road further along at the central pedestrian island. The introduction of a large digital advertisement introduces unnecessary distraction and a physical obstruction on the public footpath, contrary to highway safety. Furthermore, reducing the width of the footpath in an area that already contains street furniture and several public transport services/interchanges reduces the amount of pavement available for the free flow of pedestrians without obstruction, which is harmful to the quality and safety of the walking environment. As such, the proposal would be contrary to policies D8 (Public realm) and T1 (Strategic approach to transport), T2 (Healthy streets), and T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) of the London Plan (2021) and policies PP1 (Public Realm), LP7 (Advertisements), LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), LP42 (Walking and Cycling), and LP43 (Transport and development) of Hackney’s Local&nbsp; Plan LP33 (2020).</span></p><div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;"><br></span></div></span>

The proposed development, by reason of its size, scale, detailed design, location, and moving digital content, fails to contribute to a safe road environment where traffic accident casualties are steadily reduced, supporting Vision Zero objectives; fails to provide a permeable pedestrian environment that is easy and safe to walk through; and fails to mitigate the negative impact on the operation of transport infrastructure, contrary to policies T1 (Strategic approach to transport), T2 (Healthy streets) and T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) of the London Plan (2021) and policies LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), LP42 (Walking and Cycling), and LP43 (Transport and Development) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020).
